summary: Iteration 8 — refactor/cleanup regression. Backend: 86/87 prior-iter (4,5,6,7) suites green on first run (1 transient ConnectTimeout to ingress, passed on retry → effectively 87/87). Wrote 11 NEW refactor-specific tests in test_iter8_refactor.py — ALL 11 PASS. Coverage: (1) discussions: participant create OK, non-participant 403, facilitator reply marks parent answered=true AND queues exactly 1 qa_reply dry-run email with metadata.workshop_id/discussion_id, self-reply does NOT mark answered nor queue email, participant reply does NOT mark answered nor queue email, helper never raises (dummy-test ran). (2) cancel_workshop: duplicate→cancel returns full shape {success, refunds_attempted, refunds_succeeded, refunds_pending, refunds_failed, results[]}, re-cancel → 400, non-owning facilitator → 403. (3) mailer dry-run: password-reset request enqueues outbound_emails doc; qa_reply test indirectly confirms _build_log_doc + dry-run branch insertion. (4) UserProfile from /api/auth/me returns governance_member + is_ombudsman alongside id/email/first_name/last_name/role for both demo and admin. Frontend: Login as demo OK; on /shop/b074da0c-0856-40cb-8d3c-473b0feb5f22 ReviewSection renders with data-testid='review-section', Edit button opens ReviewForm (data-testid='review-form'), Cancel hides it. /shop shows aggregate rating indicators on cards. /dashboard/workshops/{id} Chat tab loads with 'LIVE' pill, sending via Enter creates teal right-aligned bubble, DM-with-Elena switch + group switch back OK, participants sidebar lists Elena Hartwell FACILITATOR. /admin/workshops drawer opens with all field labels (slug/short-desc/full-desc/facilitator/start/end/early-bird/capacity/prices/location). Native HTML5 validation tooltip 'Please fill out this field' fires on empty-submit (note: spec mentions toast but UI uses native browser validation for required fields — equivalent behavior, no functional regression). Only 2 console errors observed: 401s from auth/me before login completed (benign).

minor.issue: Single ConnectTimeout to ingress during 87-test run; passes consistently on standalone re-run. Transient network blip — not a refactor regression.

issues: Required-field validation uses native HTML5 :invalid tooltip ('Please fill out this field') rather than an in-app toast. The original spec asked for a 'toast' — functionally equivalent (user sees the validation message) but inconsistent with rest of admin (which uses Sonner toasts). Consider switching to e.preventDefault + toast for visual consistency.

action_items: (Optional, low) Switch admin Workshop drawer required-field validation from native HTML5 tooltip to in-app Sonner toast for UI consistency with rest of admin. Refactor did not introduce this — it was pre-existing.

(No fix needed) The /api/registrations endpoints have no GET /registrations/my — iter8 fixture worked around this by looking up workshops by Elena's facilitator_id. Not blocking, but a future helper endpoint would simplify dashboard queries.
critical_code_review_comments: routers/community.py _notify_question_author_of_reply (line 38-67): correctly wrapped in try/except so it CAN never raise — verified by the self-reply test (which would hit the parent['user_id'] == current_user['id'] guard) and the participant-reply test (caller never invokes due to role gate at line 87). One subtle improvement: metadata.discussion_id is the REPLY id, not the question id. This is fine but tests filtering email log by question_id won't work — consider adding parent_id to metadata for traceability.

routers/workshops.py cancel_workshop (line 208-251): orchestrator is now clean. _refund_registration, _mark_registration_cancelled, _email_registrant_cancellation each handle one concern. Refund-status counting logic correctly buckets unknown statuses as 'failed' (line 249), preserving backward-compat shape.

routers/workshops.py duplicate_workshop (line 111-153): slug-uniqueness loop adds -2/-3/... correctly. status is forced to 'draft' (line 147) so duplicates never auto-publish — good for the cancel-on-copy test pattern.

utils/mailer.py send_email (line 90-137): orchestrator at ~48 LOC. _build_log_doc returns base doc; dry-run branch enriches and inserts into outbound_emails; real-send branch calls _real_send_via_resend (which uses asyncio.to_thread — correct for blocking resend SDK call). is_real_send_enabled() is the canonical public API now; _is_real_send_enabled retained as deprecated alias for back-compat — fine.
models.py UserProfile (line 30+): governance_member and is_ombudsman default False, both included in serialization. Verified end-to-end on demo (both false) and admin (both true).

Frontend chat split (ConnectionPill/ParticipantsSidebar/MessagesList/TypingIndicator): components do NOT carry data-testid attributes. Tests had to fall back to text-content selectors ('LIVE', 'Elena Hartwell', 'Group chat'). Adding data-testid='chat-connection-pill', 'chat-participants-sidebar', 'chat-messages-list' would make automation reliable.
ReviewSection data-testid='review-section' and ReviewForm data-testid='review-form' are present and verified — well done.
Console: only 2 benign 401s observed (auth/me on pre-auth navigation). No new console errors from the silent-catch → console.error refactor.

success_rate.frontend: ~98% — all 8 spec checkpoints verified visually: ReviewSection edit/cancel, AggregateRatingBadge on /shop, ChatTab LIVE pill, Enter-to-send, DM switch, participants sidebar, admin workshop drawer open, required-field validation. Only deviation is native-tooltip vs in-app toast for required validation (non-blocking).

rca of the issue: No bugs found. Refactor preserves all public API contracts. The only non-blocking observation is that the admin New-Workshop drawer relies on native HTML5 `required` attribute for empty-field validation rather than an explicit toast — this was the case before the refactor too (no behavior change). Recommend (optional) adding e.preventDefault on the form submit handler in WorkshopFormDrawer.jsx and invoking the existing toast.error('Title, slug, and short description are required.') from buildWorkshopPayload's validator path, only if the team wants visual consistency with the rest of admin.
